fields.description: The opaque docname series. Nothing about the branch, the date or the subject goes in the primary key.
fields.label: Series

fields.description: The headline, as it appears in a person's notification list. Plain text, rendered as a string, because an announcement is written by staff and read by everybody the branch serves: markup typed here must not become markup running in a reader's browser.
fields.label: Title

fields.description: How the society classifies this announcement for its own purposes: news, advisory, weather warning, whatever vocabulary it keeps. A configurable set, and no code anywhere branches on a value of it. Behaviour comes from urgency next to it, which is a closed set the server owns. Optional, because a society that does not classify its announcements should not be made to.
fields.label: Type

fields.description: How loudly this should arrive, and the only field here that changes what the server does. routine: it waits in the notification list. important: it is marked out in the list and is offered email by default. urgent: the same, and it stays at the top of the list until it is read. This is a closed, code-owned set rather than a society's vocabulary, because each value names a delivery behaviour and a society adding a fourth would produce an announcement nothing knows how to deliver. Nothing compares this value in scattered places: notifications/services/announce.py holds one dispatch table keyed by it, the same shape as the member module's approval_mode.
fields.label: Urgency

fields.description: ACC-02. Which part of the society is speaking, and therefore who hears it. An announcement reaches this node and everything beneath it, so a national office anchored at the top reaches everybody and a branch reaches its own people. Required, because an announcement nobody can be resolved for is a message that goes nowhere, and because an unplaced record is invisible to geo scoping.
fields.label: From

fields.description: Which of the people beneath that node should receive this. everyone: every volunteer and every member. volunteers: people with an active volunteer record. members: people holding an active membership. A closed, code-owned set for the same reason as urgency: each value names a query the server has to know how to run. Somebody who is both a volunteer and a member is resolved once and receives one copy, never two.
fields.label: Audience

fields.description: One line summarising the announcement, shown under the title in the list before anybody opens it. Optional. Left empty, the list shows the opening of the body instead, so a writer who has nothing extra to say is not made to repeat themselves.
fields.label: Summary

fields.description: The announcement in full. Plain text, deliberately, and rendered as a string wherever it is shown. A rich text field here would mean a person able to write announcements could put scripts into a page served to every volunteer in the society, and the ability to broadcast is not the same permission as the ability to run code in somebody's browser.
fields.label: Body

fields.description: The wording on the button, if this announcement points somewhere. Left empty while a destination is set, the button reads as a plain instruction to open the link rather than showing a bare address.
fields.label: Link Label

fields.description: Where the announcement points, if anywhere. Optional. Refused on save unless it is site-relative or an http, https, mailto or tel address, the same rule content blocks are held to: a broadcast that reaches everybody is exactly the wrong place to allow a javascript or data address.
fields.label: Link

fields.description: Draft: still being written, and delivered to nobody. Published: fanned out to everybody the audience resolved to. Publishing is idempotent, so saving a published announcement again delivers nothing twice, and it is one-way: an announcement people have already read cannot be unsent, and pretending otherwise by reverting this field would leave copies in their lists that nothing owned.
fields.label: Status

fields.description: Whether this also goes out as an email, on top of appearing in the notification list. Defaults on for an important or urgent announcement and off for a routine one, which is the default rather than the rule: whoever writes it decides, and an advisory that must reach somebody who has not signed in this week needs the email.
fields.label: Also send as email

fields.description: When this was published. Written by the fan-out, not by whoever is typing, so the ordering people see is the order things actually went out in.
fields.label: Published On

fields.description: The day after which this stops appearing in people's lists. Optional, and it is a display rule rather than a deletion: a weather advisory for next Tuesday is noise on Wednesday, but the record of having sent it stays. Left empty, the announcement does not expire.
fields.label: Expires On

fields.description: How many people this actually reached. Written by the fan-out. Worth showing, because an announcement that resolved to nobody is the failure this system fails at silently otherwise: the message was written, saved and published, and read by no one.
fields.label: Delivered To
